stem: In the figure, line \(AB\) is parallel to line \(CD\). Line \(GH\) intersects the two lines at points \(E\) and \(F\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Angle \(BEF\) and angle \(DFE\) lie between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal, so they are same-side interior angles.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary: \(x + 70 = 180\), so \(x = 110\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(90 - 70\); the two angles are supplementary (sum 180°), not complementary.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This assumes the two angles are equal. They are same-side interior angles, so they add up to 180°.
explanation.C: Correct. Same-side interior angles are supplementary: \(180 - 70 = 110\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(2 \cdot 70\), an arithmetic slip; no angle relationship doubles the 70° angle here.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['A'][1]==P['B'][1] and P['C'][1]==P['D'][1]
assert abs(ang('B','E','F')-70)<0.1 and abs(ang('D','F','E')-110)<0.1
ans=180-70
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==110
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
